question: 我正在为多光谱成像相机设计一片可见-近红外双波段分光膜。要求可见光波段 450-650 nm 尽可能高的反射率（用于 RGB 通道成像），同时近红外波段 700-1000 nm 尽可能高的透过率（用于 NIR 通道），降低通道间串扰。请在 45 度入射、熔融石英基底条件下，仅使用 TiO2 和 SiO2 设计一个平面多层介质膜，膜系总层数不超过 24 层。

metrics.rationale: The user explicitly requests '尽可能高的反射率' (highest possible reflectance) for the visible band '450-650 nm' to support RGB imaging.
The user explicitly requests '尽可能高的透过率' (highest possible transmittance) for the near-infrared band '700-1000 nm' to support NIR imaging.

standard.metric_rationale: This set directly translates the user's dual-band dichroic requirement into two complementary objectives: maximizing reflection in the visible range and maximizing transmission in the NIR range. By optimizing both simultaneously, the solver is forced to find a design that separates these bands, which inherently addresses the user's goal to '降低通道间串扰' (reduce channel crosstalk). The angle of 45 degrees is applied to both metrics as specified. No additional metrics (like minimizing transmission in the visible or reflection in the NIR) are included because maximizing the primary desired observable in each band implicitly suppresses the unwanted observable due to energy conservation (R+T+A=1, with A≈0 for dielectric stacks), keeping the metric count minimal and focused on the explicit performance goals.
standard.formula_rationale: The user explicitly demands two independent performance goals: maximizing visible reflectance for RGB imaging and maximizing near-infrared transmittance for NIR imaging. Since the request treats both bands as equally critical for the dual-band functionality and provides no reason to prioritize one channel over the other, the expression simply sums the two metrics. This ensures that a design is only ranked highly if it performs well in both regions simultaneously, directly reflecting the goal of reducing crosstalk by enforcing high efficiency in both the reflection and transmission bands.

route.title: Visible-High-Reflector with NIR-Transmission Window Optimization
route.scientific_hypothesis: A dielectric stack composed of alternating TiO2 and SiO2 layers, optimized for constructive interference in the 450-650 nm band at 45 degrees incidence, will inherently provide high transmittance in the 700-1000 nm band, and fine-tuning individual layer thicknesses can minimize spectral crosstalk at the band edge more effectively than a standard quarter-wave design.
route.design_principle: Distributed Bragg Reflection: Alternating layers of high (TiO2) and low (SiO2) refractive index materials create a photonic stopband where reflectance is high. The center wavelength and bandwidth of this stopband are determined by the optical thickness of the layers. By deviating from exact quarter-wave thicknesses, the spectral slope at the band edge can be engineered to separate the visible reflection band from the NIR transmission band.
route.proposed_topology: Substrate (Fused Silica) | [TiO2, SiO2] repeated 12 times | Air. Total coating layers: 24. Sequence starts with TiO2 adjacent to the substrate.
design_variables: Individual thickness of each of the 24 layers (24 independent variables)
Layer sequence order is fixed as alternating High-Low starting with High
soft_objectives: Maximize the sharpness of the transition between 650 nm and 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count strictly limited to 24
Materials restricted to TiO2 and SiO2
Deposition precision required for non-quarter-wave thicknesses
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory for multilayer dielectric stacks
Transfer Matrix Method for calculating spectral response at oblique incidence (45 degrees)
Concept of photonic bandgaps in periodic media
expected_advantages: Full utilization of the allowed 24-layer budget to achieve steep spectral cut-on/cut-off
Simultaneous optimization of both s and p polarization responses at 45 degrees
Potential to exceed standard quarter-wave performance by tailoring field distribution
known_risks: Optimization may converge to a local minimum with poor polarization balance
Extreme thickness variations might be difficult to manufacture uniformly
Side lobes in the reflection band might reduce NIR transmission if not constrained
route.execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer planar dielectric coating on a fused silica substrate using only TiO2 (Siefke) and SiO2 (Gao). The stack sequence is fixed as 12 pairs of (TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao)), starting with TiO2 (Siefke) next to the substrate. Optimize the physical thickness of all 24 layers independently to maximize reflectance in the 450-650 nm band and maximize transmittance in the 700-1000 nm band at 45 degrees angle of incidence. The optimization should consider unpolarized light or equally weight s and p polarizations. The incident medium is air. Do not change the material order or the number of layers; only vary the thicknesses.

route.title: 24-Layer Chirped Dichroic Optimization
route.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing the layer count from 20 to the maximum allowed 24 and initializing with a chirped (graded) thickness profile will allow the optimizer to broaden the high-reflection band edges and improve NIR transmission compared to the uniform 20-layer baseline.
route.design_principle: Chirped mirrors use varying layer thicknesses to reflect different wavelengths at different depths, effectively widening the reflection bandwidth. Applying this to a dichroic filter should smooth the transition between the visible stopband and NIR passband.
route.proposed_topology: Fused Silica Substrate | (TiO2 | SiO2) x 12 | Air
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
expected_advantages: Wider reflection bandwidth due to chirp
known_risks: Chirped initialization might converge to a solution with lower peak reflectance if the gradient is too steep
route.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer dielectric stack on a fused silica substrate using TiO2 and SiO2. The layer sequence must be strictly alternating starting with TiO2. Initialize the optimizer with a linearly chirped thickness profile where the first pair is tuned for 650 nm (quarter-wave) and the last pair for 450 nm (quarter-wave), with intermediate layers interpolated linearly. Optimize all 24 layer thicknesses to maximize reflectance in 450-650 nm and transmittance in 700-1000 nm at 45 degrees incidence for unpolarized light. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 450-650 nm, 700-1000 nm. soft objectives: high reflectance in 450-650 nm band; high transmittance in 700-1000 nm band; minimized spectral crosstalk between bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 450-650 nm band; reflectance in 700-1000 nm band. manufacturing constraints: maximum 24 layers; materials restricted to TiO2 and SiO2.
route.revision_reason: Increases layer count to 24 and changes initialization from periodic/uniform to chirped to address feedback regarding bandwidth and local optima.
